title: The Upstream Watch
tagline: A morning check on code I borrow, with a warning if it looks tampered with.
what: A watch list of the outside code my projects are built on, plus a script that checks every entry each morning for new releases, new code and signs of tampering.
built: Built a list of nearly 400 outside projects, each noting what I use it for and which of my projects needs it
Made a private copy of nearly all of them on my own server, synced every 6 hours
Wrote a tamper check: a release that suddenly points at different code, or rewritten history, gets flagged first
Added screening: known malware accounts are refused, brand-new or little-known ones get a caution label
credit: I wrote it from scratch; the code it watches belongs to other people.
starring: Me, and every project of mine that borrows code

making.problem: I build on a lot of other people's code, and I wanted to hear when they improved it. Then the next question was: how do I know an update is safe to take?
how: Anything I clone or fork gets queued for the list automatically, and I add the rest by hand.
Each morning a script reads every project's releases and newest code, and compares them with the last run.
What changed goes to my Discord, grouped by which of my projects uses it, with anything that looks tampered with at the top.
Taking an update is always my call.

moment.what: The watch flagged two releases of a Mario Kart 64 port for the 3DS: both suddenly pointed at different code. I dug in. The author had rewritten the whole history to change one text file, and the downloads were untouched. Real alarm, harmless cause.

run: - mario-kart-64-3ds: tag v2.0, v2.1-E1 now points at different code
(re-tagged after release). Do not take this release until someone has read why.
Nothing updates by itself: upstream changes are reviewed and cherry-picked on purpose.
